english: Considering the principal value of $\cos^{-1}$, for each non-negative integer $n$ let $I_{n}=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}x^{n}\cos^{-1}x\,dx$. If $I_{6}=\dfrac{p}{q}$, where $p$ and $q$ are positive integers with $\gcd(p,q)=1$, then the value of $p+q$ is ______.
hindi: $\cos^{-1}$ के मुख्य मान को लेते हुए, प्रत्येक अऋणात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना $I_{n}=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}x^{n}\cos^{-1}x\,dx$ है। यदि $I_{6}=\dfrac{p}{q}$ है, जहाँ $p$ तथा $q$ धनात्मक पूर्णांक हैं तथा $\gcd(p,q)=1$ है, तो $p+q$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Integrate by parts with $u=\cos^{-1}x$, $dv=x^{n}dx$: $I_n=\left[\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\cos^{-1}x\right]_0^{1}+\dfrac{1}{n+1}\int_0^{1}\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$. The bracket is $0$ at both ends ($\cos^{-1}1=0$ and $x^{n+1}=0$ at $0$).

So $I_n=\dfrac{1}{n+1}J_{n+1}$, where $J_m=\int_0^{1}\dfrac{x^{m}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$. With $x=\sin\theta$ ($\theta:0\to\frac{\pi}{2}$), $J_m=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{m}\theta\,d\theta$, a Wallis integral, so $J_m=\dfrac{m-1}{m}J_{m-2}$.
Reduction formula for $I_n$: $(n+1)I_n=J_{n+1}=\dfrac{n}{n+1}J_{n-1}$ and $J_{n-1}=(n-1)I_{n-2}$, so $I_n=\dfrac{n(n-1)}{(n+1)^{2}}I_{n-2}$ for $n\ge2$.
originality_note: New: moments of cos^-1 x, where one integration by parts turns them into Wallis integrals of the next order, giving a two-step reduction with squared denominators (way 1). Closest known: reduction formulas for int x^n sin^-1 x dx and int_0^{pi/2} sin^n x dx. Different because: the link to Wallis appears only after integrating the inverse function, and the reduction in n has the unusual factor n(n-1)/(n+1)^2.

concept_use.Integration by reduction: Integration by parts gives I_n = J_{n+1}/(n+1) and the reduction I_n = n(n-1)/(n+1)^2 I_{n-2}.
concept_use.Walli's theorem in Integration: J_m = int_0^{pi/2} sin^m theta d theta after x = sin theta; Wallis' formula gives J_7 = 16/35.

key_step: Integrate by parts so that I_n = J_{n+1}/(n+1), then use Wallis (or the derived reduction) for J_7.
justification: Two linked ideas: by parts on an inverse trigonometric function leading to a Wallis integral, and a reduction formula; exact fraction arithmetic with no options. Lighter than 2021-P2-Q12 (L4); L3.
